title: Students and staff protest university funding levels in Vienna

tea.why: Students and university employees protested against planned education spending cuts and government funding levels for public universities.
tea.want: Protesters demanded increased university budgets to cover inflation costs and prevent cuts to educational programs and working conditions.
tea.changed: Oct 23: News sources reported on the large demonstration held the previous day in Vienna, following a federal government funding decision.

summary: Thousands of students, employees, and members of the academic community marched through central Vienna to protest against government plans for higher education funding for 2028–2030. Organised by the Austrian National Union of Students under the slogan “Red Alert – #SaveTheUniversities!”, the demonstration opposed a federal budget allocation of €16 billion, which participants argued falls short of the €18 billion needed to offset inflation. University administrations supported the action by allowing students and staff to participate. In response, the federal government maintained that the €16 billion amount is final following an agreement reached by senior officials.
demands: Ensure adequate resources to cover inflation costs
response: The federal government stated that the €16 billion budget allocation for 2028–2030 is final following an agreement reached by senior officials, according to sources.

crowd.text: At least 30,000 people attended the rally, police said.

updates.text: Thousands of students and staff marched in Vienna to protest university funding levels.
